tasks.title: Implement the ET trading-day/holiday calendar service incl. the ESC-023 New Year's year-end exception (D16)
tasks.description: Create the pure, Qt-free services/market_calendar.py exposing is_trading_day(date), trading_days(start_ts, end_ts) and session_windows(start_ts, end_ts, ext_hours), with US equity holidays computed by rule (fixed-date, nth-weekday, Good Friday) in America/New_York. Ship its offscreen unit tests. Corrected for ESC-023: the New Year's observed shift carries the NYSE Rule 7.2 year-end accounting-period exception (AC-D16.7) so Dec 31 stays a trading day when the next Jan 1 is a Saturday, and no substitute closure is created.
acceptance_criteria: Given the ET trading calendar, When is_trading_day is called for a US equity holiday computed by rule (fixed-date New Year's Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Christmas; nth-weekday MLK, Presidents, Memorial, Labor, Thanksgiving; Good Friday), Then it returns False for each such date in a given year including a future year, proving no fixed year list.
Given the ET trading calendar, When is_trading_day is called, Then an ordinary weekday with no holiday (e.g. 2026-09-21) returns True and a Saturday or Sunday returns False.

Given the US-equity ET trading-day calendar, When is_trading_day is called for a weekend-falling fixed-date US holiday, Then the observed market-closure day is non-trading per US-equity convention, EXCEPT that New Year's Day carries the NYSE Rule 7.2 year-end accounting-period exception (ESC-023, AC-D16.7): when Jan 1 is a Saturday no New Year's closure is observed and Dec 31 of that year returns True as a trading day (e.g. 2021-12-31, 2027-12-31, 2032-12-31, 2038-12-31), while Independence Day 2026-07-04 Sat gives 2026-07-03 Fri closed, Christmas 2022-12-25 Sun gives 2022-12-26 Mon closed, Juneteenth 2027-06-19 Sat gives 2027-06-18 Fri closed, and New Year's Day 2023-01-01 Sun is still observed Mon 2023-01-02 closed.

Given a start_ts and end_ts spanning at least one week, When trading_days(start_ts, end_ts) is called, Then it returns exactly the ET trading days in the inclusive range, ascending, excluding every weekend and every holiday.

Given a range spanning trading and non-trading days, When session_windows(start_ts, end_ts, ext_hours) is called, Then it returns one window per trading day, 04:00-20:00 ET when ext_hours is True and 09:30-16:00 ET when ext_hours is False, clipped to [start_ts, end_ts], with no window for a non-trading day.
Given services/market_calendar.py, When it is imported in an offscreen process, Then it imports no PyQt6, pyqtgraph or other Qt module and needs no QApplication.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the ET trading calendar, When is_trading_day is called for a US equity holiday computed by rule (fixed-date New Year's Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Christmas; nth-weekday MLK, Presidents, Memorial, Labor, Thanksgiving; Good Friday), Then it returns False for each such date in a given year including a future year, proving no fixed year list.
tests.description: Parameterized holiday dates for each by-rule holiday across at least two years including a future year; assert is_trading_day returns False.
tests.expected_result: Every listed holiday date returns False, including a future-year date and the Good Friday date derived for that year.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the ET trading calendar, When is_trading_day is called, Then an ordinary weekday with no holiday (e.g. 2026-09-21) returns True and a Saturday or Sunday returns False.
tests.description: Check one ordinary weekday and the adjacent weekend days in ET.
tests.expected_result: 2026-09-21 (Monday) returns True; 2026-09-19 (Saturday) and 2026-09-20 (Sunday) return False.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the US-equity ET trading-day calendar, When is_trading_day is called for a weekend-falling fixed-date US holiday, Then the observed market-closure day is non-trading per US-equity convention, EXCEPT that New Year's Day carries the NYSE Rule 7.2 year-end accounting-period exception (ESC-023, AC-D16.7): when Jan 1 is a Saturday no New Year's closure is observed and Dec 31 of that year returns True as a trading day (e.g. 2021-12-31, 2027-12-31, 2032-12-31, 2038-12-31), while Independence Day 2026-07-04 Sat gives 2026-07-03 Fri closed, Christmas 2022-12-25 Sun gives 2022-12-26 Mon closed, Juneteenth 2027-06-19 Sat gives 2027-06-18 Fri closed, and New Year's Day 2023-01-01 Sun is still observed Mon 2023-01-02 closed.
tests.description: Assert the observed-shift behaviour in tests/test_market_calendar.py: keep the unchanged weekend-falling closure shifts (Independence Day 2026-07-03, Christmas 2022-12-26, Juneteenth 2027-06-18, New Year's 2023-01-02) as non-trading regression guards, and assert the New Year's year-end exception - is_trading_day is True for 2021-12-31, 2027-12-31, 2032-12-31 and 2038-12-31 (Jan 1 Saturday -> no New Year's closure; Dec 31 stays open), with the Saturday legal date 2022-01-01 non-trading as a weekend and 2022-01-03 a trading day. Drop the wrong date(2021, 12, 31) entry from the weekend-legal-dates loop.
tests.expected_result: is_trading_day(2026-07-03) is False, (2022-12-26) is False, (2027-06-18) is False, (2023-01-02) is False; is_trading_day(2021-12-31) is True and likewise for 2027-12-31, 2032-12-31, 2038-12-31; is_trading_day(2022-01-01) is False and (2022-01-03) is True; no assertion expects a Dec 31 year-end closure.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a start_ts and end_ts spanning at least one week, When trading_days(start_ts, end_ts) is called, Then it returns exactly the ET trading days in the inclusive range, ascending, excluding every weekend and every holiday.
tests.description: Call trading_days over a week that contains a US holiday and assert the exact ascending set.
tests.expected_result: Returns exactly the non-holiday weekdays for that range in ascending order, with the weekend and holiday absent.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a range spanning trading and non-trading days, When session_windows(start_ts, end_ts, ext_hours) is called, Then it returns one window per trading day, 04:00-20:00 ET when ext_hours is True and 09:30-16:00 ET when ext_hours is False, clipped to [start_ts, end_ts], with no window for a non-trading day.
tests.description: Call session_windows with ext_hours True and False over a multi-day range including a weekend/holiday; check window count, ET boundaries and clipping.
tests.expected_result: One window per trading day: 04:00-20:00 ET (ext_hours True) or 09:30-16:00 ET (ext_hours False), each clipped to the range; no window for a non-trading day.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given services/market_calendar.py, When it is imported in an offscreen process, Then it imports no PyQt6, pyqtgraph or other Qt module and needs no QApplication.
tests.description: Import the module in an isolated offscreen interpreter and assert no Qt module is loaded (or assert the source imports no PyQt6/pyqtgraph).
tests.expected_result: Import succeeds without QApplication and without importing PyQt6/pyqtgraph.

tasks.title: Implement the pure missing-span and chunk-request planner (D16)
tasks.description: Create the pure, Qt-free services/backfill_service.py with bar_period_seconds(timeframe), find_missing_spans(cached_ts, now_ts, timeframe) and plan_requests(missing_spans, timeframe), plus the MissingSpan/RequestPlan dataclasses. Detection is trading-day presence so internal holes and tail gaps are both healed; empty cache returns [] and chunking uses the TIMEFRAME_CONFIG duration, newest chunk first, with a Qt-free UTC hyphenated anchor. Ship its offscreen unit tests.
acceptance_criteria: Given each of the six timeframes, When bar_period_seconds(timeframe) is called, Then it returns the per-bar period from data.bar_aggregator.TIMEFRAME_SECONDS (1 min 60, 5 mins 300, 15 mins 900, 1 hour 3600, 4 hours 14400, 1 day 86400).

Given a seeded cached ts series with bars before and after a missing trading-session span (the reported internal hole), When find_missing_spans(cached_ts, now_ts, timeframe) is called, Then it returns the missing span(s), merging adjacent missing trading days and excluding weekends/holidays; the assertion is parameterized over all six timeframes and at least two distinct seeded series scenarios.

Given a seeded cached series whose newest bar is before now (tail gap), When find_missing_spans is called, Then the missing trading days between the last cached trading day and now are returned as a span.
Given a cached series whose latest trading day already reaches now, or whose only gap is a weekend, When find_missing_spans is called, Then it returns [] so no redundant backfill is requested.
Given an empty cache (cached_ts == []), When find_missing_spans is called, Then it returns [] so the caller falls back to the configured window.

Given a missing span whose duration exceeds TIMEFRAME_CONFIG[timeframe]['duration'], When plan_requests(missing_spans, timeframe) is called, Then it returns multiple RequestPlans ordered newest chunk first whose combined coverage spans the whole missing span, each carrying the timeframe bar_size and duration and an endDateTime in the UTC hyphenated yyyyMMdd-HH:mm:ss format, with successive anchors stepping back by one configured duration.
Given a missing span shorter than the configured duration, When plan_requests is called, Then it returns exactly one RequestPlan covering the span with the anchor at the span end.
Given services/backfill_service.py, When imported offscreen, Then it imports no PyQt6/pyqtgraph/Qt and does not require a live IBKR connection.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given each of the six timeframes, When bar_period_seconds(timeframe) is called, Then it returns the per-bar period from data.bar_aggregator.TIMEFRAME_SECONDS (1 min 60, 5 mins 300, 15 mins 900, 1 hour 3600, 4 hours 14400, 1 day 86400).
tests.description: Parameterized call over the six timeframes comparing against TIMEFRAME_SECONDS.
tests.expected_result: Each timeframe returns the matching period in seconds.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a seeded cached ts series with bars before and after a missing trading-session span (the reported internal hole), When find_missing_spans(cached_ts, now_ts, timeframe) is called, Then it returns the missing span(s), merging adjacent missing trading days and excluding weekends/holidays; the assertion is parameterized over all six timeframes and at least two distinct seeded series scenarios.
tests.description: For each of the six timeframes and two seeded series (internal hole spanning a weekend), assert find_missing_spans covers exactly the missing weekdays and merges adjacent missing days.
tests.expected_result: Exactly the missing trading-weekday span(s) are returned; weekend days are excluded and adjacent missing days are merged into one span.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a seeded cached series whose newest bar is before now (tail gap), When find_missing_spans is called, Then the missing trading days between the last cached trading day and now are returned as a span.
tests.description: Seed a series ending mid-week with now several trading days later.
tests.expected_result: The span covers every trading day after the last cached day up to now (weekends excluded).

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a cached series whose latest trading day already reaches now, or whose only gap is a weekend, When find_missing_spans is called, Then it returns [] so no redundant backfill is requested.
tests.description: Two cases: cache current at now, and cache ending Friday with now on Sunday.
tests.expected_result: Both cases return an empty list.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given an empty cache (cached_ts == []), When find_missing_spans is called, Then it returns [] so the caller falls back to the configured window.
tests.description: Call find_missing_spans with an empty cached ts list.
tests.expected_result: Returns [].

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a missing span whose duration exceeds TIMEFRAME_CONFIG[timeframe]['duration'], When plan_requests(missing_spans, timeframe) is called, Then it returns multiple RequestPlans ordered newest chunk first whose combined coverage spans the whole missing span, each carrying the timeframe bar_size and duration and an endDateTime in the UTC hyphenated yyyyMMdd-HH:mm:ss format, with successive anchors stepping back by one configured duration.
tests.description: Give a span longer than one configured duration and assert chunk count, newest-first order, full coverage, duration/bar_size and anchor format.
tests.expected_result: Chunk count equals the configured-duration ceiling of the span; plans are newest-first; together they cover the span; anchors parse as UTC yyyyMMdd-HH:mm:ss and step back by one duration.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a missing span shorter than the configured duration, When plan_requests is called, Then it returns exactly one RequestPlan covering the span with the anchor at the span end.
tests.description: Give a short missing span and assert a single plan whose anchor is at the span end.
tests.expected_result: Exactly one RequestPlan covering the span, anchor at the span end.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given services/backfill_service.py, When imported offscreen, Then it imports no PyQt6/pyqtgraph/Qt and does not require a live IBKR connection.
tests.description: Import the module in an isolated offscreen interpreter and assert no Qt module is loaded and no connection is attempted.
tests.expected_result: Import succeeds without QApplication and without importing PyQt6/pyqtgraph or contacting TWS.

tasks.title: Make the MainWindow load path backfill the whole gap with correlated multi-request orchestration (D16)
tasks.description: Change ui/main_window.py::load_chart to call the pure planner and issue one req_historical_data per RequestPlan through the existing endDateTime parameter (market_data.py signature unchanged), skip redundant requests when the cache is current, fall back to the configured window on an empty cache, add _history_req_ids/_history_generation/_backfill_missing_spans/_backfill_failed_req_ids state, accept any member reqId, finalise once when the set empties, cancel every id on switch/close, and correlate _on_error shortfall without fabricating bars. Ship focused offscreen load-path tests.
acceptance_criteria: Given a seeded cached series with a missing trading-session span whose closure exceeds the timeframe configured fetch window, When load_chart runs, Then it issues one historical request per planned chunk through the existing req_historical_data(endDateTime=...) (the market_data.py signature is unchanged) and records each returned reqId in _history_req_ids.
Given an empty plan and a cache whose latest bar reaches now, When load_chart runs, Then no historical request is issued for that load (no redundant request).
Given an empty cache, When load_chart runs, Then the configured-window fallback request (endDateTime empty) is issued so the single-request path is preserved as a set of one.

Given a backfill wave with multiple in-flight reqIds, When _on_historical_bar/_on_historical_data_end fire for any member, Then bars accumulate across all members and BarCache.save_bars plus re-read plus ChartPanel.update_chart happen exactly once, only after the last member's end empties the set; a non-member or stale-generation event is ignored.

Given backfill requests in flight, When the symbol/timeframe switches or closeEvent runs, Then every reqId in _history_req_ids is cancelled and _history_generation is advanced so late responses cannot mix symbols/timeframes.

Given a backfill reqId raises error_msg, When _on_error handles it, Then the reqId is removed from _history_req_ids so the wave can still finalise, and the shortfall is surfaced (status bar plus log) with no fabricated bar.

Given a wave completes and a trading day in the target span is still empty, When finalisation runs, Then the shortfall is surfaced explicitly (status-bar message and/or log); no bar is fabricated or interpolated.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a seeded cached series with a missing trading-session span whose closure exceeds the timeframe configured fetch window, When load_chart runs, Then it issues one historical request per planned chunk through the existing req_historical_data(endDateTime=...) (the market_data.py signature is unchanged) and records each returned reqId in _history_req_ids.
tests.description: Offscreen MainWindow with IBApiClient.connect monkeypatched and md_manager.req_historical_data stubbed to capture calls and return distinct reqIds; seed a BarCache with an internal hole; call load_chart.
tests.expected_result: The number of req_historical_data calls equals the planner chunk count; every call passes a non-empty endDateTime; every returned reqId is present in _history_req_ids.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given an empty plan and a cache whose latest bar reaches now, When load_chart runs, Then no historical request is issued for that load (no redundant request).
tests.description: Seed a cache current at now, stub req_historical_data as a spy, call load_chart.
tests.expected_result: req_historical_data is never called and no reqId is added to _history_req_ids.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given an empty cache, When load_chart runs, Then the configured-window fallback request (endDateTime empty) is issued so the single-request path is preserved as a set of one.
tests.description: Seed no cached bars; call load_chart with a stubbed manager.
tests.expected_result: Exactly one fallback request is issued with an empty endDateTime and behaves as a set of one.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a backfill wave with multiple in-flight reqIds, When _on_historical_bar/_on_historical_data_end fire for any member, Then bars accumulate across all members and BarCache.save_bars plus re-read plus ChartPanel.update_chart happen exactly once, only after the last member's end empties the set; a non-member or stale-generation event is ignored.
tests.description: Drive _on_historical_bar for each member reqId, then _on_historical_data_end for all but the last, then for the last; spy on save_bars/update_chart; also emit a non-member and a stale-generation bar.
tests.expected_result: No save/render before the set empties; exactly one save plus one re-read plus one update_chart at set-empty; non-member and stale-generation bars are ignored.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given backfill requests in flight, When the symbol/timeframe switches or closeEvent runs, Then every reqId in _history_req_ids is cancelled and _history_generation is advanced so late responses cannot mix symbols/timeframes.
tests.description: Start a multi-request wave, then switch symbol/timeframe (and separately invoke closeEvent); spy on cancel_historical_data and read the generation token.
tests.expected_result: cancel_historical_data is called once per tracked id; the generation token advances; late responses from the previous generation do not reach the render path.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a backfill reqId raises error_msg, When _on_error handles it, Then the reqId is removed from _history_req_ids so the wave can still finalise, and the shortfall is surfaced (status bar plus log) with no fabricated bar.
tests.description: Raise _on_error for one member reqId mid-wave, then end the remaining members and assert finalisation still occurs and a shortfall message is shown.
tests.expected_result: The failed reqId leaves _history_req_ids; the wave finalises when the rest end; a status-bar/log shortfall is emitted and no bar is fabricated for the failed chunk.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a wave completes and a trading day in the target span is still empty, When finalisation runs, Then the shortfall is surfaced explicitly (status-bar message and/or log); no bar is fabricated or interpolated.
tests.description: Complete a wave whose responses omit one target trading day; assert the shortfall is surfaced and the rendered bars contain no fabricated entries.
tests.expected_result: A shortfall status-bar/log message is produced and the bar list contains only genuinely returned bars.

tasks.title: Cancel and finalise the backfill wave on disconnect or a stalled request so the shortfall is surfaced (D16 / ESC-024)
tasks.description: Extend the existing D16 backfill-wave lifecycle in ui/main_window.py so a silent transport drop or a request that never yields historical_data_end can no longer strand the wave. On _on_disconnected (and on a bounded wave timeout), drop every tracked backfill reqId, cancel it, advance _history_generation so late responses are ignored, and finalise exactly once through the existing _finalize_history_wave so the AC-D16.4 shortfall (status bar + log) IS surfaced, with no bar fabricated. Ship focused offscreen tests.
acceptance_criteria: Given a multi-request backfill wave is in flight (load_chart has registered more than one reqId in _history_req_ids), When the connection drops (_on_disconnected fires) before any historical_data_end arrives, Then every tracked reqId is dropped from _history_req_ids, cancel_historical_data is called for each, and _history_req_ids is empty afterwards.

Given the same disconnect, When _on_disconnected fires mid-wave, Then _history_generation is advanced so that a late historical_data_end / historical_bar for a pre-drop reqId is rejected by _history_event_accepted and neither finalises the wave nor accumulates bars (no double finalise, no late contamination).

Given the wave is stranded by a disconnect (or a bounded timeout) with trading sessions in _backfill_missing_spans still empty in the cache, When the wave finalises, Then _finalize_history_wave runs exactly once and surfaces the outstanding shortfall explicitly (status bar message and log) — the 'incomplete'/'missing' shortfall path of AC-D16.4 — rather than leaving a silent hole.
